title: Three ways down a gradient
caption: Oxygen, small and non-polar, diffuses straight through the lipid. Potassium ions are charged, so they need a channel; glucose is large and polar, so it needs a carrier. All three move down their own gradients, so none of them uses ATP.
alt: A phospholipid bilayer with oxygen diffusing straight through it, potassium ions leaving through a channel protein and glucose entering through a carrier protein, each with the concentration on either side.
description: Oxygen: 0.05 outside, 0.02 inside; it crosses the bilayer by simple diffusion.
Potassium ions: 140 inside, 4 outside; they leave through a potassium channel.
Glucose: 5 outside, 0.5 inside; it enters on a GLUT carrier protein.
Concentrations are typical values in mmol per dm³.
